gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-kay-pho-du: Marker-bold and sunlit, Red Hat Display draws each curve with daylight inside, while Kay Pho Du lays a hollow-reed serif beneath it. That pairing of old and new is its best trick.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-labrada: Labrada reads dignified and bookish, its small letters opening wide, while Red Hat Display keeps one steady pen pressure from first letter to last. Its strongest quality is that clear split.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-laila: Laila is a text serif with generous gaps between its curve ends and stems, giving it a traditional, editorial voice. And Red Hat Display does the opposite job best, holding a constant stroke width that feels bold and modern.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-libertinus-ser: Libertinus Serif is a refined text serif, with a slight swell on the bowls and hairlines that thin at the curves. But Red Hat Display stays ruler-straight in weight, and that firm, authoritative gap between them is the draw.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-libre-caslon-t: Libre Caslon Text reads editorial and refined, its thick-thin variation low-key, like a round brush barely pressed. And Red Hat Display sets wire-like, tubular letterforms above it, so the page moves from tight tubing to soft brushwork.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-lustria: Red Hat Display draws as if with a fixed pen, every stroke the same. Lustria, a classic serif, then adds middle-ground contrast and a wide-mouthed lowercase a, so the page shifts from marker line to modest weight changes.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-maitree: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display holds a single-width stroke in every glyph, with daylight inside each curve. And Maitree, a classic serif, carries a mild stress in its o and e, so a longer passage reads dignified and unhurried.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-marcellus: Marcellus has subtle weight changes like etched lines in glass, with rounded letters that stay clearly open on one side. And Red Hat Display, pencil-like and never thickening, leads into a longer passage that feels refined and literary.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-montaga: Thread-stitched and a touch bookish, Montaga leaves its pen-lifted curves unfinished beneath the bold, contemporary lines of Red Hat Display. A longer passage in this text serif reads editorial and soft.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Red Hat Display draws like a marker, with one constant line and bold, contemporary punch. But Nanum Myeongjo, a classic serif, does its best work in a restrained thick-thin rhythm, with curve tips that never quite touch.
